accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes ISRO's RLV-TD ‘Pushpak’?
o: A reusable winged vehicle intended to support a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system
A single-use solid-propellant launch vehicle for lunar missions
A cryogenic upper stage used in the GSLV Mk II
A reusable capsule designed exclusively for crewed re-entry
accepted.x: Pushpak is ISRO’s reusable winged vehicle and is intended to contribute to a Two-Stage-To-Orbit system.
accepted.tq: Use the exact vehicle-purpose association rather than confusing it with a launcher stage.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: The RLV-TD ‘Pushpak’ completed which of the following experiments?
o: Integrated hot test of a semi-cryogenic engine
accepted.x: Pushpak completed LEX-03, an autonomous landing experiment.
accepted.tq: Match the named vehicle with its specific test or mission.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated benefit of reusable launch systems?
o: Elimination of the need for thermal protection systems
Reduction in launch cost by up to 80 percent
accepted.x: Reusable vehicles require a reusable Thermal Protection System; its elimination is not a benefit identified for such systems.
accepted.tq: Find the option that reverses a stated benefit into an impossibility.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding reusable launch systems:
1. Autonomous precision landing is one of the technological challenges.
2. High research and development cost is a challenge.
3. Reusable Thermal Protection Systems are required.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements identify challenges associated with reusable launch systems.
accepted.tq: Check each statement against the separate challenge categories before choosing the combined code.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: New Glenn is associated with Blue Origin. Falcon 9 and Starship belong to SpaceX, while Zhuque-3 belongs to LandSpace.
accepted.tq: Start with the company–vehicle pair that is directly identifiable and eliminate swapped-company options.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer.

accepted.s: Which reusable rocket is associated with first-stage recovery more than 520 times?
accepted.x: Falcon 9’s first stages had been recovered more than 520 times as stated.
accepted.tq: Link the distinctive numerical figure with the correct vehicle rather than with another reusable rocket.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about Starship is correct?
o: It uses approximately 1,200 tonnes of liquid methane and LOX and is fully reusable.
Its booster is recovered only by parachute.
It is an orbital-class recovery vehicle developed by LandSpace.
It uses refined kerosene and LOX and has no planned in-orbit refuelling.
accepted.x: Starship is described as fully reusable and using about 1,200 tonnes of liquid methane and LOX.
accepted.tq: Separate the vehicle’s propellants and reusability from the characteristics of other rockets.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: How many in-orbit refuellings are needed by Starship for NASA’s Moon-landing mission, as indicated?
accepted.x: Starship is indicated to require more than 10 in-orbit refuellings for NASA’s Moon-landing mission.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an approximate threshold from an exact numerical claim.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: Which company developed Zhuque-3, associated with attempted recovery of orbital-class stages?
accepted.x: Zhuque-3 is associated with LandSpace of China.
accepted.tq: Use the developer–vehicle association and avoid confusing it with the two SpaceX vehicles.
accepted.sec: Reusable launch systems - RLV-TD, Pushpak, foreign reusable rockets

accepted.s: Agnilet, developed by Agnikul Cosmos, is described as the world’s first:

o: Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre’s private pad
Dhanush, India’s first private launch pad at Sriharikota
Satish Dhawan Space Centre’s second launch pad
A private launch pad at Bengaluru

accepted.s:
Which of the following statements about Agnite is correct?
1. It is a single-piece 3D-printed booster engine.
2. It is made of Inconel.

solid motor for the Agnibaan booster

accepted.s: ISRO’s 1,000-hour life test was conducted on which propulsion system?
o: A 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster of the Hall type
accepted.x: The test involved a 300 mN Stationary Plasma Thruster, a Hall-type thruster using xenon.
accepted.tq: Match the test duration and thrust rating to the correct propulsion technology.

accepted.s: Which propellant is used in the Hall-type Stationary Plasma Thruster tested by ISRO?
accepted.x: The Hall-type Stationary Plasma Thruster uses xenon as its propellant.
accepted.tq: Discriminate the electric-propulsion propellant from chemical rocket propellants.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: The specific impulse of the tested Hall-type thruster is approximately how many times that of chemical systems?
accepted.x: Its specific impulse is approximately six times that of chemical propulsion systems.
accepted.tq: Recall the distinctive comparative figure rather than the absolute thrust value.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: The Hall-type Stationary Plasma Thruster is intended to replace chemical propulsion on future:
accepted.x: The thruster is intended for replacing chemical propulsion on future communication satellites.
accepted.tq: Connect the propulsion technology with its stated operational application.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: Which company demonstrated an indigenous green propulsion system?
accepted.x: Bellatrix Aerospace demonstrated an indigenous green propulsion system.
accepted.tq: Identify the private company associated with the specific demonstration.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: Why is LOX-methane considered important for Mars-return missions and in-situ resource utilisation?
o: It can be stored indefinitely without refrigeration.
Methane can be produced from Martian resources, while the combination is cleaner and cheaper.
LOX-methane is a hypergolic combination that ignites on contact.
Methane has the highest density of all cryogenic fuels and needs no oxidiser.
accepted.x: LOX-methane is considered cleaner and cheaper, and methane can be produced from Martian resources.
accepted.tq: Use the cause–application link instead of confusing methane with hypergolic or earth-storable propellants.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: POEM is correctly expanded as:
accepted.x: POEM stands for PSLV Orbital Experimental Module.
accepted.tq: Test the exact expansion of the acronym and avoid substitutions of similar space terms.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: What is the principal function of the spent PS4 stage in POEM?
o: It is used as a planetary landing engine.
It is converted into a reusable crew capsule.
It is reused as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
It serves as a cryogenic upper stage for GSLV.
accepted.x: POEM reuses the spent PS4 stage as an orbital platform for start-up and academic payloads.
accepted.tq: Follow the transformation of the spent stage into its orbital-platform role.
accepted.sec: Green and electric propulsion - green propellants, Hall thrusters, POEM

accepted.s: In a cryogenic engine, the fuel and oxidiser are respectively:
accepted.x: Cryogenic propulsion uses liquid hydrogen as fuel and liquid oxygen as oxidiser.
accepted.tq: Keep the fuel–oxidiser order distinct from the reverse order and from semi-cryogenic combinations.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly gives the approximate temperatures of liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen?
accepted.x: Liquid hydrogen is approximately −253°C, while liquid oxygen is approximately −183°C.
accepted.tq: Watch the reversed-number trap in paired temperature values.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s: The exhaust of a liquid hydrogen–liquid oxygen cryogenic engine is predominantly:
accepted.x: The exhaust is described as only water vapour because hydrogen combines with oxygen.
accepted.tq: Infer the exhaust from the chemical composition of the propellants.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s: Which characteristic of cryogenic propulsion is correctly stated?
o: It uses dense kerosene and is non-toxic.
It has a specific impulse of approximately 260 seconds and cannot be restarted.
It is unsuitable for upper stages because of its low efficiency.
It has a specific impulse of approximately 450 seconds, the highest among the listed categories.
accepted.x: Cryogenic propulsion has an approximate specific impulse of 450 seconds and is the most efficient category listed.
accepted.tq: Associate the highest specific impulse with cryogenic propellants, not solid or semi-cryogenic systems.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s: Why are liquid hydrogen cryogenic systems unsuitable for military missiles?
o: Liquid hydrogen has an exceptionally high density and requires no insulation.
Liquid hydrogen has very low density, about 0.071 g/ml, requires huge tanks and is difficult to store for long periods.
Liquid hydrogen cannot produce water vapour on combustion.
Liquid hydrogen ignites spontaneously on contact with nitrogen tetroxide.
accepted.x: The very low density of liquid hydrogen, about 0.071 g/ml, necessitates large tanks and makes long-term storage difficult.
accepted.tq: Link the numerical density with the storage and tank-size consequence.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Cryogenic Upper Stage Project began in 1994.
2. The project cost was ₹300 crore.
3. India tested a full cryogenic stage in 2006.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: The Cryogenic Upper Stage Project began in 1994, involved a cost of ₹300 crore, and India tested a full cryogenic stage in 2006.
accepted.tq: Treat the project date, cost and test milestone as independent factual checks.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s: What was the outcome of the 1991 Glavkosmos agreement concerning cryogenic technology?
o: Russia transferred all cryogenic technology without restriction.
The United States supplied seven cryogenic engines to India.
US MTCR-based sanctions stopped technology transfer, although Russia supplied seven engines.
The agreement was cancelled by India before any engines were supplied.
accepted.x: Glavkosmos agreed to sell engines and technology in 1991, but US MTCR-based sanctions in 1992 stopped technology transfer; Russia supplied seven engines only.
accepted.tq: Separate the original agreement, the later sanctions and the limited engine supply.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s:
Arrange the following events in chronological order:
A. Glavkosmos agreed to sell cryogenic engines and technology.
B. MTCR-based sanctions stopped the technology transfer.
C. India tested a full cryogenic stage.
D. GSLV Mk II flew with the indigenous CE-7.5 stage.
accepted.x: The sequence is 1991 agreement, 1992 sanctions, 2006 full-stage test and 2014 GSLV Mk II flight with the indigenous stage.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last events by year, then place the sanctions and test between them.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s: GSLV Mk II flew with the indigenous CE-7.5 cryogenic stage on:
accepted.x: The indigenous CE-7.5 cryogenic stage was flown by GSLV Mk II on 5 January 2014.
accepted.tq: Distinguish adjacent-year options using the exact milestone date.
accepted.sec: Cryogenic technology - propellants, uses, countries, GSLV, Russian deal, MTCR

accepted.s: Which engine is correctly matched with its propellant combination and application?
o: Vikas — UH25 and N2O4 — PSLV second stage
CE-7.5 — kerosene and LOX — GSLV Mk II upper stage
CE-20 — solid fuel and liquid oxidiser — LVM3 C25 stage
SE2000 — LOX and LH2 — NGLV upper stage
accepted.x: Vikas uses UH25 and N2O4 and is used in the PSLV second stage. CE-7.5 and CE-20 use LOX and LH2, while SE2000 uses kerosene and LOX.
accepted.tq: Start with the engine–propellant pair and then verify its vehicle stage.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s: The CE-7.5 engine is associated with which combination?
o: 75 kN, LOX–LH2 staged-combustion engine for the GSLV Mk II cryogenic upper stage
UH25–N2O4 engine for the PSLV second stage
200 kN, LOX–LH2 gas-generator engine for the LVM3 C25 stage
Semi-cryogenic kerosene–LOX engine for the NGLV
accepted.x: CE-7.5 is a 75 kN staged-combustion LOX–LH2 engine used in the GSLV Mk II cryogenic upper stage.
accepted.tq: Combine thrust rating, engine cycle and stage application to reject mixed attributes.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s: Which statement regarding CE-20 is correct?
o: It is a 75 kN staged-combustion engine used in GSLV Mk II.
It is a solid motor used in the PSLV first stage.
It is a kerosene–LOX engine replacing the L110 core.
It is a 200 kN-class gas-generator LOX–LH2 engine used in the LVM3 C25 upper stage.
accepted.x: CE-20 is a 200 kN-class gas-generator LOX–LH2 engine for the LVM3 C25 upper stage.
accepted.tq: Separate CE-20 from CE-7.5 using cycle, thrust and vehicle-stage clues.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s:
The CE-20 engine has been used for which of the following missions or flight categories?
1. Chandrayaan-2
2. Chandrayaan-3
3. All LVM3 commercial flights
accepted.x: CE-20 powers the LVM3 C25 upper stage used for Chandrayaan-2, Chandrayaan-3 and all LVM3 commercial flights.
accepted.tq: Check whether the engine association extends across all three listed applications.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s: What is the significance of the CE-20 bootstrap-mode start test?
o: It eliminates the need for liquid oxygen in the engine.
It proves that CE-20 can operate only with solid propellant.
It demonstrates starting on the engine’s own propellant flow without external gas, supporting in-space restart.
It converts CE-20 into a hypergolic engine.
accepted.x: Bootstrap mode starts the engine using its own propellant flow without external gas and is important for in-space restart capability.
accepted.tq: Connect the test method with its operational consequence rather than with a propellant change.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s: Which propellant combination is planned for the SE2000 engine?
accepted.x: SE2000 is a semi-cryogenic engine using refined kerosene and LOX.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the semi-cryogenic combination from the cryogenic and earth-storable pairs.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s: SE2000 is planned for which applications?
o: Replacing the C25 in GSLV Mk II only
The PSLV first stage and S200 booster only
Replacing the L110 in LVM3-SC and for the NGLV
accepted.x: SE2000 is planned for LVM3-SC, replacing the L110, and for the NGLV.
accepted.tq: Match the engine with its planned vehicle-stage applications.
accepted.sec: Rocket engines → propellant combination

accepted.s: Which propellant category is correctly matched with its characteristic?
o: Solid — high initial thrust but cannot normally be throttled or stopped
Hybrid — cannot be stopped or restarted
Hypergolic — requires an external ignition system at every start
Cryogenic — least efficient but simplest to handle
accepted.x: Solid propellants provide high initial thrust but generally cannot be throttled or stopped. Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact, hybrids can be stopped or restarted, and cryogenic systems are highly efficient but complex.
accepted.tq: Compare the operational feature of each propellant category instead of relying on the category name alone.
accepted.sec: Propellant categories - examples

accepted.s: Which one of the following is an earth-storable liquid propellant combination?
accepted.x: UH25 and N2O4 are listed as earth-storable liquid propellants. Refined kerosene and LOX are semi-cryogenic, while LH2 and LOX are cryogenic.
accepted.tq: Separate earth-storable liquid propellants from cryogenic and semi-cryogenic combinations.
accepted.sec: Propellant categories - examples

accepted.s: Hydrazine-family propellants combined with N2O4 are classified as hypergolic because they:
o: Are non-toxic and suitable for large reusable boosters
Require cryogenic storage and have the highest specific impulse
Ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring
accepted.x: Hypergolic propellants ignite on contact and are useful for spacecraft manoeuvring, although they are highly toxic.
accepted.tq: Use the defining property of hypergolic propellants to identify the correct application.
accepted.sec: Propellant categories - examples

accepted.s:
Which of the following is correctly matched?
1. HTPB — solid propellant example
2. Hydrazine, MMH and UDMH — earth-storable liquid examples
3. Kerosene and LOX — semi-cryogenic combination
4. Solid fuel and liquid oxidiser — hybrid combination
accepted.x: All four pairings are correct examples of the respective propellant categories.
accepted.tq: Verify each category–example pair before selecting the complete combination.
accepted.sec: Propellant categories - examples

accepted.s: Which propellant category has an approximate specific impulse of 260 seconds and is associated with high initial thrust?
accepted.x: Solid propellants have an approximate specific impulse of 260 seconds and provide high initial thrust.
accepted.tq: Use the specific-impulse figure as the discriminator among propellant categories.
accepted.sec: Propellant categories - examples

accepted.s: Which statement best describes hybrid propulsion?
o: It uses solid fuel and a liquid oxidiser and can be stopped or restarted.
It uses hydrazine and N2O4 and ignites on contact.
It uses liquid hydrogen and liquid oxygen and is the most efficient category.
It uses UH25 and N2O4 and cannot be restarted.
accepted.x: Hybrid propulsion combines solid fuel with a liquid oxidiser and can be stopped or restarted.
accepted.tq: Identify the category from its distinctive two-phase propellant arrangement and controllability.
accepted.sec: Propellant categories - examples

accepted.s: The SE2000 semi-cryogenic engine uses:
o: Refined kerosene as fuel and LOX as oxidiser
Liquid hydrogen as fuel and LOX as oxidiser
HTPB as fuel and liquid oxygen as oxidiser
UH25 as fuel and N2O4 as oxidiser
accepted.x: SE2000 uses refined kerosene and liquid oxygen.
accepted.tq: Test the exact fuel–oxidiser pairing of the named semi-cryogenic engine.
accepted.sec: Semi-cryogenic engine - propellants and tests

accepted.s: What did the third hot test of the SE2000 Power Head Test Article validate?
o: Autonomous landing of a reusable vehicle
Ignition and start-up at 60 percent power
Operation with liquid hydrogen at 100 percent power
In-space restart at full power without propellant flow
accepted.x: The third hot test of the PHTA at 60 percent power validated ignition and start-up.
accepted.tq: Combine the test number, power level and validated functions to avoid partial matches.
accepted.sec: Semi-cryogenic engine - propellants and tests

accepted.s: Which private company conducted a static test of the KALAM 1200 solid motor?
accepted.x: Skyroot’s KALAM 1200 solid motor was static-tested at SDSC-SHAR.
accepted.tq: Match the private company with its specific motor and test activity.
accepted.sec: Semi-cryogenic engine - propellants and tests

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes Skyroot’s KALAM 1200 motor?
o: An 11-metre solid motor containing 30 tonnes of propellant
A 30-metre semi-cryogenic engine containing 11 tonnes of propellant
An 11-metre cryogenic engine containing 30 tonnes of liquid hydrogen
A 1200 kN Hall thruster tested with xenon
accepted.x: KALAM 1200 is described as an 11-metre solid motor with 30 tonnes of propellant.
accepted.tq: Watch for reversal of the dimensions and propellant quantity in the options.
